claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends maintaining a signal-to-noise ratio of at least 10 dB(A) and a minimum Speech Transmission Index of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges.
source_title: ACRP Research Report 175 — Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems, Chapter 3 (Speech Intelligibility)
supporting_excerpt: The study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges.
denominator: PA broadcast performance at listener position
caveat: Report is guidance, not a mandatory code; adoption requires local design-manual incorporation.

claim: IEC 60268-16 defines the Speech Transmission Index framework for objective rating of speech intelligibility, with qualitative categories: Bad (<0.30), Poor (0.30–0.45), Fair (0.45–0.60), Good (0.60–0.75), Excellent (>0.75).
source_title: IEC 60268-16:2020 — Sound system equipment, Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines the STI model, test signals, measurement and prediction methods for sound system equipment.
airport_or_entity: International standard (used at airports and other venues)
denominator: modulation-transfer function of the transmission channel
caveat: Paywalled standard; full technical text requires purchase from IEC/ANSI.

claim: The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (PL 118-63) held the Passenger Facility Charge cap at $4.50 (unchanged since 2000) and authorized AIP at approximately $4 billion annually through FY2028.
source_title: Congressional Research Service — The 2024 Federal Aviation Administration Reauthorization (IF12791)
supporting_excerpt: The PFC cap remains at $4.50 per enplaning passenger... AIP authorized at $4 billion annually through FY2028.
units: USD per enplaned passenger; USD billions per year
denominator: per-passenger PFC cap; annual AIP authorization
caveat: Authorization does not equal appropriation; annual appropriations may vary within the authorization.
